rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-1: the requirements cost some current and would-be inspectors more than they would otherwise spend (55% hold no certification, 40% carry no insurance, 34% cannot be grandfathered).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-3: despite complaint-only enforcement, unlicensed practice is deterred for most inspections (agents' forms and lenders ask for the license number; buyers and agents complain).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-2: some incumbents who cannot be grandfathered train and sit the exam to stay in practice.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-16: some unlicensed practice continues where complaint is least likely (pre-listing and builders' inspections, Linmouth inspectors in the border metro).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-9: some buyers at the margin go without an inspection or use an unlicensed inspector when the fee rises (cash investors, buyers of new homes with builders' warranties).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-4: the training and exam bear on competence that buyers value and cannot easily judge.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-17: agents, schools and the inspectors' association can organize at a cost below their stake.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-055 (illustrative figures), A-18: without the Act the inspectors' association would have kept lobbying for licensing (campaign since 2022). A-31 (p 0.6) says agents and schools would not have lobbied; the question asks about the contest the policy text records, which is the association's campaign.
